avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 induction may significantly reduce riluzole levels and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative mood support if needed

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate neurotoxic effects and increase hepatotoxicity risk with riluzole
avoid_supplements.action: Limit to <400 IU/day or discontinue; discuss with prescriber

caution_supplements.name: NAC (N-acetylcysteine)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate glutamate pathway effects; additive neuroprotective claims lack strong evidence
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased side effects; use only under medical supervision

caution_supplements.name: Curcumin/Turmeric
caution_supplements.mechanism: Minor CYP3A4 inhibition may slightly increase riluzole exposure
caution_supplements.action: Monitor liver function tests; maintain consistent intake if used

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases riluzole bioavailability and hepatotoxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Completely avoid grapefruit and related citrus fruits; choose alternative beverages

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase riluzole absorption and GI side effects
caution_foods.action: Take riluzole consistently with or without food; maintain same timing pattern

caution_foods.name: Charred/grilled foods (high PAH content)
caution_foods.mechanism: May induce CYP1A2, potentially reducing riluzole levels
caution_foods.action: Maintain moderate intake; excessive consumption may reduce efficacy

monitoring_notes: Riluzole carries hepatotoxicity risk; monitor baseline and periodic liver function tests (ALT/AST) every 3 months. Counsel patients to report jaundice, dark urine, or abdominal pain immediately and avoid all potent CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers.
